sections.title: The skill → effect → buff chain
sections.summary: A hero skill can only express a narrow fixed vocabulary on its own combat_skill line; everything richer lives in the buff system, and the effect is the bridge that lets a skill apply a buff.
points: A combat_skill line alone reaches only: accuracy, damage %, move, launch/target, use-limits, is_continue_turn, ignore_stealth/guard.
Persistent stat changes, resistances, conditional "only-while-X" modifiers, DoT-magnitude tweaks, and stress/heal-received scaling all live in the buff system, not on the skill line.
The effect is the bridge: a skill fires effects, and an effect can apply a buff — so the chain is skill → effect → buff.
This chain is precisely how a hero skill gains attributes "normally reserved for buffs" that it could never do alone.
Link points: combat_skill .effect "X" ↔ effect: .name "X" ↔ effect .buff_ids "id" ↔ buffs.json "id".
All names are resolved by rolling-hash lookup against the effect/buff registries; an unmatched name silently no-ops (no error outside debug). A typo does nothing.

examples.code:
combat_skill: .id "bulwark_of_faith" … .effect "Cru Bulwark Resist"
  ↓
effect: .name "Cru Bulwark Resist" .target "performer" .buff_ids "cru_bul_res_stun cru_bul_res_debuff"
  ↓
shared/buffs/overhaul.buffs.json:
  { "id":"cru_bul_res_stun", "stat_type":"resistance", "stat_sub_type":"stun",
    "amount":0.15, "duration_type":"combat_end" }
examples.note: The full reference chain: skill names an effect, the effect applies named buff(s), the buff carries the real power. Each arrow is a string → hash lookup.

sections.title: The four ways an effect carries a buff (mutually exclusive)
sections.summary: An effect can carry a buff four ways, but they are mutually exclusive — pick exactly one per effect; the validator counts them and errors on more than one.
points: .buff_ids "a b c" applies up to 8 NAMED buffs, reaches all 93 stat_types + resistances + lifecycle, is rule-gateable, and requires a buffs.json entry. This is THE bridge for buff-only powers.
Inline .combat_stat_buff 1 + .<stat>_add/_multiply is an anonymous quick stat buff reaching only the 10 combat stats, no rule gate, no buffs.json needed.
Inline .buff_type + .buff_sub_type + .buff_amount is one anonymous combat-stat buff (combat stats only), no rule gate, no buffs.json.
.riposte <n> (+ .riposte_effect) is the riposte special case, reaching riposte state only.

The inline forms are a convenience for a plain timed combat-stat swing; the moment a skill needs anything conditional, resistance-based, DoT-modifying, or from the wider stat palette, it must go through a named buff.
Exclusivity is validator-enforced: exactly one of buff_ids / combat_stat_buff(+mutators) / buff_type / riposte per effect; more than one errors.

sections.title: What a named buff unlocks that skills/inline effects CANNOT reach
sections.summary: The whole reason the bridge exists: capabilities that have no skill field and no inline effect field, reachable only by applying a buffs.json entry.
points: Conditional stats — the 55 rule_type gates ("only while below 50% HP", "only vs Eldritch", "only in rank 1", "while stealthed", "first round only", "at Death's Door", "while target is burning"…). Skill lines and inline combat_stat_buff are unconditional; only a named buff carries rule_type (+ is_false_rule to invert). This is the single biggest unlock.

Resistances — stat_type: resistance (buff stun/bleed/blight/disease/move/debuff/death_blow/trap for a duration). Skills have no resistance field and inline combat_stat_buff reaches only the 10 combat stats, not the resistance domain. A resist buff is only achievable via buff_ids.

The wider stat palette — DoT magnitude/duration mods (hp_dot_bleed_amount_percent…), stress_dmg_percent / stress_dmg_received_percent, hp_heal_received_percent, apply-chances (bleed_chance, stun_chance…), cure-chances, ignore_protection / ignore_guard, damage_reflect_percent, deathblow_chance, and regen (hp_dot_heal) — all are buff stat_types, none expressible inline.

Duration semantics + lifecycle — duration_type (combat_end battle-banner, permanent, quest_end) plus lifecycle flags: remove_if_not_active (strip the buff any turn its rule goes false — pairs with a conditional rule), consume_on_rule_active, clear_buffs_on_rule_active, is_clear_debuff_valid (set false so an enemy can't cleanse your self-buff), force_positive.

sections.title: Targeting — who receives the buff
sections.summary: The effect's .target picks the recipient; the buff's rule (if any) then evaluates against that actor.
points: .target "performer" → self-buff (an hpbelow rule tests the caster's HP).
.target "target" → debuff on the enemy (a target_is_burning rule tests the enemy).
.target "performer_group" → the whole party (party-wide banner).
So a "gains +crit while below half HP" self-buff = a performer-targeted effect applying a buff whose rule_type is hpbelow, rule_data.float 0.5.

sections.title: Mechanics (code-backed)
sections.summary: How buff_ids parse and apply at the code level, plus the free reuse of vanilla buffs.
points: .buff_ids parses up to 8 space/quote-delimited tokens, each hashed → pushed into the effect's buff-id vector (effect+0x68).
At apply time the effect grants those buffs to its .target; each buff then lives on its own rule + duration, independent of the skill that delivered it.
Exclusivity (validator): exactly one of buff_ids / combat_stat_buff(+mutators) / buff_type / riposte per effect.

Reuse vanilla buffs for free: naming a base-game buff id in .buff_ids (e.g. a shared resist buff or a TRINKET_* buff) inherits its exact behavior + tooltip with no new authoring. The overhaul reuses vanilla effect AND buff ids this way.

sections.title: Worked examples (shipped, in-game-verified Crusader)
sections.summary: Three concrete Crusader patterns showing why the bridge is required: a battle-long resistance, a heal-over-time regen, and a conditional crit buff.
points: Bulwark of Faith rank 3 grants three resistance buffs at duration_type combat_end (battle-long stun/debuff/move resist) — no skill field exists for this; the buff is the only route.
Second Wind applies buff cru_regen_1 = {stat_type:"hp_dot_heal", amount:2, duration_type:"combat_end"}; regen is a buff stat_type, not a skill/effect field.

Conditional-buff pattern "+15% crit while below half HP": a performer-targeted effect applying {stat_type:"combat_stat_add", stat_sub_type:"crit_chance", amount:0.15, rule_type:"hpbelow", rule_data:{float:0.5}}; the hpbelow gate is inexpressible on a skill line or inline effect — buff-only.

examples.note: Bulwark of Faith rank 3 — three resistance buffs a skill physically cannot grant, all duration_type combat_end.
Second Wind — heal-over-time regen, a buff stat_type not reachable on a skill/effect field.

examples.code:
{ stat_type:"combat_stat_add", stat_sub_type:"crit_chance", amount:0.15,
  rule_type:"hpbelow", rule_data:{ float:0.5 } }
examples.note: Conditional +15% crit while below half HP — the hpbelow rule gate is buff-only.

sections.title: When inline is enough (don't over-reach for buff_ids)
sections.summary: A plain timed combat-stat swing with no condition is cleanest inline, needing no buffs.json entry.
points: A plain timed combat-stat swing with no condition — e.g. "+8% dodge for this battle" — is cleanest inline.
Reach for .buff_ids the moment you need a rule gate, a resistance, or any non-combat-stat stat_type.

examples.note: "+8% dodge for this battle" done inline — no buffs.json entry required.

sections.title: Trinket trigger firing model (§8)
sections.summary: A trinket reaches the same effect→buff bridge through a second, richer door: 22 event triggers, each a JSON array of effect names under <trigger>_additional_effects; the engine runs those effects at the named moment.
points: Skills reach the bridge through combat_skill .effect "X"; a trinket has 22 event triggers, each a JSON array of effect NAMES under key <trigger>_additional_effects (e.g. "round_end_additional_effects": ["My Regen Pulse"]).

At the named moment the engine runs those effects, and from there the effect→buff chain is identical — this is how a trinket does conditional, event-driven effects a static buffs list can't (DoT-on-being-hit, heal-on-kill, self-destroy on death).

Accessor FUN_140471ee0(trinketEntry, &outVec, triggerIndex, targetHint) returns the entry's effect-id vector for one of the 22 triggers; combat reads stored vectors by index, not the name table 0x142ac9740 (that table is load + tooltip only).

Generic firing helper FUN_1405fce10(bg, wearer, source, target, triggerIndex, groupFlag) finds the wearer's trinket, pulls the vector, and enqueues each id via FUN_1405fd0f0(bg, source, target, effectId).
In FUN_1405fd0f0: source → effect-record source, target → effect-record target — the effect's .target "target" resolves to whatever actor the firing site passes as target.
groupFlag 1 = scan the hero party for the wearer, 0 = scan the monster group. Two group lists on the battleground object: bg+0x8 = hero party, bg+0x48d0 = monster group.

For 7 triggers the firing site injects the target itself (a specific per-member or self actor), so the effect must be authored .target "target" — the loader warns otherwise (a warning, not a reject; per-trigger flag byte at entry+0x45). Forced set: kill_all_heroes(9), kill_all_monsters(10), was_killed_all_heroes(11), was_killed_all_monsters(12), was_hit_all_heroes(14), was_hit_all_monsters(15), on_dodge(18).
For the other 15, the wearer id is passed only as a hint and the effect's authored .target decides (performer self-buff, target the enemy, this_trinket self-modify) — the standard §4 targeting model.

examples.note: A trigger key is a JSON array of effect names; the engine runs those effects at round end, then the effect→buff chain proceeds normally.

sections.title: Trinket trigger gotchas (§8D)
sections.summary: Author-facing non-obvious behaviors of the trinket trigger family.
points: "all_" = one firing per living member, not a group-object apply. kill_all_heroes loops the hero list and applies your effect to each hero individually as target. To hit the whole party you write ONE effect with .target "target"; the engine fans it out.
was_hit_all_heroes/_monsters (14/15) are wearer-relative, chosen by the victim's side: 14 = all allies of the wearer, 15 = all enemies of the wearer (a monster wearing it flips them).
By contrast kill_all (9/10) and was_killed_all (11/12) are hard-wired hero (bg+0x8) / monster (bg+0x48d0) with no swap.

Self-target triggers (6, 8, 17, 21, and 18) pass source=target=the wearer — a performer-targeted effect and a target-targeted effect land on the same actor, but .target "target" is the safe choice for the forced set (18).

These are trinket-ENTRY only. A trinket set bonus has none of this machinery — its only way to fire an effect is the attack_additional_effect_ids carrier-buff escape hatch (on-attack only, rule-gated).

triggers.name: Kill All Heroes
triggers.event: Wearer kills → once per living hero
triggers.notes: Evidence 1406052b0:105. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Hard-wired hero list (bg+0x8), no side swap. Fans out one firing per living hero.

triggers.name: Kill All Monsters
triggers.event: Wearer kills → once per living monster
triggers.notes: Evidence 1406052b0:114. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Hard-wired monster list (bg+0x48d0), no side swap. Per-member firing.

triggers.name: Was Killed — All Heroes
triggers.event: Wearer is killed → per living hero
triggers.notes: Evidence 1406056a0:214. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Hard-wired hero list, no side swap.

triggers.name: Was Killed — All Monsters
triggers.event: Wearer is killed → per living monster
triggers.notes: Evidence 1406056a0:226. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Hard-wired monster list, no side swap.

triggers.name: Was Hit
triggers.event: Wearer is hit (hit path, not dodge)

triggers.name: Was Hit — All Heroes
triggers.event: Wearer is hit → per member of wearer's ally group
triggers.notes: Evidence 1405ad470:259. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Wearer-relative = all allies of the wearer (flips if a monster wears it).

triggers.name: Was Hit — All Monsters
triggers.event: Wearer is hit → per member of the enemy group
triggers.notes: Evidence 1405ad470:274. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Wearer-relative = all enemies of the wearer (flips if a monster wears it).

triggers.name: On Dodge
triggers.notes: Evidence 1405ade50:74,115. Forced-target set: must author .target "target". Self-target but in the forced set, so .target "target" is the safe choice.

triggers.name: On Quest Complete
triggers.event: Quest completes (out of combat; counted by quest_uses)

triggers.name: Was Killed
triggers.notes: Evidence 1406056a0:176. Free-target trigger; also drives was_killed_all_heroes/_monsters.

triggers.name: Round End
triggers.target_binding: Self, fires for every wearer on both sides
